title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous and next pages): there is a group extension (3) 1 → π → π̃ → C → 1, with C presumably cyclic of finite order. ρ ∈ π̃ is a chosen splitting element, and ρ(x) = ρxρ^{-1} denotes the induced automorphism of π. Every other splitting element over the same element of C has the form ρ'_g = gρ with g ∈ π. Condition (6) on ρ' then becomes an equation (8) on g; for an involution this reads gρ(g) = 1, the cocycle condition. π acts on splittings by conjugation. Translated to g, this is the ρ-twisted conjugation (10) θ_ρ(α): g ↦ αgρ(α)^{-1}. So conjugacy classes of splittings correspond to twisted classes of solutions of (8), which is the non-abelian H^1(C, π).

This page addresses the 'transporter' question. For fixed solutions g, g', consider the set of α ∈ π with g' = αgρ(α)^{-1}, which he calls the ρ-transporters of g into g'. It is a coset αΠ(ρ,g) of the stabilizer Π(ρ,g) = {β : βgρ(β)^{-1} = g}. Unwinding ρ(β) = ρβρ^{-1}, the condition becomes β(gρ)β^{-1} = gρ. Hence the stabilizer is the centralizer π^{ρ'_g} of the splitting element ρ'_g = gρ in π, i.e. the fixed points of int(ρ'_g) on π (14). Consequently α is unique iff π^{ρ'_g} = 1 (15). This condition depends only on the conjugacy class of the splitting ρ'_g.

The purpose is to describe the set of conjugacy classes of splittings (e.g. of 'complex-conjugation-like' involutions) in the extension relevant to the 'équation des lacets'. One also wants to know when the conjugating element is unique, i.e. to rigidify the identification. The next page extends the action to all of π̃ and shows that π̃-classes coincide with π-classes.
errors: No mathematical errors. Only a convention point: the set αΠ(ρ,g) is called a 'classe à droite' (right coset). In current convention this is a left coset, but French usage of the time varied.

ideas.what: Conjugacy classes of splittings of π → π̃ → C correspond to twisted-conjugacy classes of solutions g of the cocycle equation, via ρ' = gρ.
ideas.modern_name: Non-abelian H^1(C, π) classifying conjugacy classes of complements/sections
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Serre, Cohomologie galoisienne; Grothendieck/Giraud non-abelian cohomology)
ideas.where_published: Standard. Treated in Grothendieck's Tôhoku-era and SGA1-type material and in Giraud; also implicit in Esquisse / Longue Marche discussions of conjugacy classes of involutions in π̂_1

ideas.what: The stabilizer of g under twisted conjugation equals the centralizer of the splitting element gρ in π. The transporters form a coset of it, with uniqueness iff the centralizer is trivial.
ideas.modern_name: Stabilizer of a twisted-conjugacy class = centralizer of the twisted cocycle; fixed subgroup π^{ρ'}

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine verification in non-abelian group cohomology of a cyclic group: twisted conjugation, with stabilizer equal to the centralizer of the corresponding section. It is careful bookkeeping toward the 'équation des lacets' with no new result on this page.
transcription_corrections: Line 3: 'Quand est-on [?] unicité de α' should read 'Quand a-t-on unicité de α'.
On this page the group is written lowercase π (not Π) throughout; Θ(α).g is written with Θ_ρ in (13).
Last lines: likely 'condition qui ne dépend que de la classe de conjugaison du scindage de (3) défini par g, i.e. par ρ'_g', not 'donnée de conjugaison … i.e. ρ = ρ'_g'.
